basics.name: Milad Mohammadi
basics.label: AI Researcher & Senior AI Engineer
basics.summary: I am an AI researcher and Senior AI Engineer with an M.Sc. in IT Engineering from the University of Tehran. I study how language agents can understand and simulate individual human behavior, connecting foundation models with psychological and cognitive frameworks. My work spans psychiatric interviewing, multilingual emotion recognition, structured reasoning, and production AI systems.

First-author PsyCIDRA preprint; second-author paper in Findings of EACL 2026; co-first-author SemEval 2025 paper.
Ranked first among 4,696 candidates in Iran’s 2023 IT Engineering master’s entrance examination.
Production language-agent and retrieval systems, alongside interdisciplinary research and graduate teaching.

work.name: IntRest
work.summary: IntRest is a Canadian startup building food-analysis software and APIs for restaurants, packaged-food brands, and food platforms. Its tools turn menus and recipes into nutrition information, allergen and diet insights, and food labels. As Senior AI Engineer, I lead the architecture and development of its AI services, from product requirements and agent design through integration and production diagnostics, working with the frontend and backend teams.
highlights: Designed and delivered 7+ AI-powered capabilities covering ingredient identification, nutrition analysis, allergens, dietary classifications, recipes, portions, and labeling.
Built a modular Python platform with separate API, domain-logic, and food-data layers, exposing typed FastAPI/Pydantic interfaces for integration with the product.
Developed food retrieval using USDA and CNF reference data, combining keyword, semantic, and hybrid search through Milvus to ground ingredient matching.
Designed language-agent workflows with validated tool outputs and deterministic fallbacks, connecting flexible language interpretation with reproducible portion and nutrient calculations.
Implemented ingredient and portion editing with automatic recalculation, alongside serving-declaration and nutrition-claim workflows that make assumptions and assessment reasons reviewable.
Improved service reliability and efficiency through local and Redis caching, duplicate-request handling, bounded concurrency, deadlines, retries, and partial-success responses.
Established regression coverage, integration documentation, and Langfuse tracing to support team handoffs and diagnose model calls, token use, and pipeline behavior.

work.name: Adan AI
work.summary: At Adan AI, I developed language-model applications for customer service and enterprise knowledge access. My work covered a banking assistant, Persian document retrieval, and tools that helped teams build and deploy FAQ chatbots.
highlights: Led architecture and delivery of a customer-service assistant for a national bank, translating product requirements into user stories and a ReAct/Reflexion workflow with more than 15 tool steps.
Implemented and reviewed LangGraph and OpenAI components and defined production evaluation metrics for the banking assistant.

Built a Persian PDF-to-RAG pipeline with table- and chart-aware parsing, chunking, and entity extraction, reducing processing costs by 50% and improving retrieval accuracy by 8 percentage points on a human-annotated evaluation set.
Developed an automated FAQ chatbot generator that cleaned Excel FAQs, expanded seed data, and deployed chatbots without manual coding, reducing onboarding from days to under one hour.

positioning.headline: Understanding people through language agents.
positioning.intro: I’m Milad Mohammadi, an AI researcher and Senior AI Engineer. I recently completed my M.Sc. at the University of Tehran, working across natural language processing and computational cognitive psychology.
positioning.researchSummary: I want to understand how foundation models can represent an individual’s personality, preferences, and changing psychological states. My research connects language-agent engineering with psychological theory and evaluation against human evidence.

interests.title: Modeling individuals
interests.description: How can language models build and revise representations of a person’s traits, preferences, and changing mental states? I am interested in models that predict new responses and remain sensitive to the person and their context.

interests.title: Behavioral simulation
interests.description: I want to build configurable simulations of human behavior for research, training, and testing human-facing systems. A central question is whether changing a psychological or social parameter produces the intended behavioral difference.

interests.title: Evaluation grounded in people
interests.description: Plausible dialogue is a starting point. I want to test psychological coherence, consistency, and correspondence to held-out human behavior, with attention to cultural variation and people who are underrepresented in training data.

interests.title: Human–agent interaction
interests.description: I am interested in how agents use interaction history, personal context, and uncertainty to support useful dialogue. My work on psychiatric interviewing provides one setting for studying these questions with domain experts.

positioning.phdIntro: I am looking for PhD opportunities at the intersection of machine learning, natural language processing, and the science of human behavior. I would like to develop and evaluate language agents with researchers in AI and psychology, building on my experience in interdisciplinary research, production systems, and teaching.
